title: Owner Auto Policy Underwriting Guideline — Household Drivers When a Named Insured Holds More Than One Open Policy
content:
When a named insured holds more than one open Owner Auto Policy, the household driver schedule is evaluated across all of them.

1. **Listing on every open policy.** Every resident of the household who has reached the household listing age must appear on each open policy, either as a rated driver or as a named excluded driver. The listing age is set in the package schedule.
2. **No rating where excluded elsewhere.** A person excluded on one open policy may not be rated on another open policy of the same named insured. This condition applies when a driver is added. It is read from the company's records of the driver's changes on the named insured's open policies, matched by the driver's name.
3. **Excluded-driver count per policy.** The count of excluded drivers is evaluated per policy, against that policy's own package maximum. It is never summed across policies.
4. **Leaving the household.** A driver removed from one policy because they left the household is removed from every open policy of the named insured, with the same change effective date.

**Points of judgement (hypothetical).**
- A named insured has two open policies, each excluding one person. Each policy is measured against its own maximum, so neither is counted as having two exclusions.
- A son excluded on the first policy cannot be added as a rated driver on the second.
